first_30_seconds.what_sticks: Haiku forms cartels as often as students but keeps them at near-monopoly prices, and told-only enforcement deters it far more, with only 2 of 7 human results reproducing.

title.why: Content is right, but 29 words with two claims and a slogan; it reads like an abstract, generalizes from one model, and buries the human-baseline design.
title.better: Fines, Leniency and Rewards on LLM Pricing Agents: A Human-Calibrated Replay of a Cartel Experiment

second_model_finding.why: For enforcement design it is the sharper finding: report-based instruments are blind when nothing is said. But it rests on 2 pools and lacks a Sonnet no-channel baseline.
second_model_finding.how_to_place: Own short subsection after the Haiku results, one panel or table row, explicitly labelled exploratory, with the missing Sonnet baseline named as a limitation.

novelty.why: Replays Bigoni et al. with LLM sellers and extends Werner's human-vs-algorithm comparison to leniency and rewards; first quantitative test of these instruments on LLMs is new, the design is not.

inconsistencies: Table 3 leniency convictions '9 (3 / 7)': detections plus reports sum to 10, not 9.
Leniency fines 2,400 points do not match 3 detections (1,200) plus 7 sole reports (1,400) = 2,600.
Table 2 caption says reward intervals collapse at the point value; Figure 1 panel 2 shows a wide interval on the reward report rate.
Figure 1 panel 7 shows the human fine cartel price near 5.0; Table 2 gives 6.14.
Text: NoReport minus fine +0.25 [+0.10, +0.40]; Figure panel 7: Fine-NoRep -0.25 [-0.41, -0.10]; sign flipped, bound differs.
Methods implies Results 7 and 8 are not testable; Results and Figure 1 score Result 7 as tested and not reproduced.
overclaims: 'A told fine deters it more than it deterred people': own placebo attributes about half of the effect to the word 'prohibited'.
'The first measurement of fines, leniency and whistleblower rewards on LLM pricing agents': priority claim the related-work search cannot guarantee.
'The shifted grid shows that recall does not drive the numbers': label shift does not test regime-level recall; leniency difference excludes zero.
'Coordination without a channel, beyond the reach of these instruments': no Sonnet no-channel or fixed-rival baseline; could be a pricing prior.
'Results 1 and 2 rest on incentives; 4 to 7 rested on human undercutting': post hoc mechanism while agents' reasons are not analysed.
'An authority can run the harness on any model before agents reach a market': shown for two Claude models in a lab game.
'The word prohibited removes about half of the fine's effect, the penalty the other half': assumes additivity from a single placebo arm.
gaps: No Sonnet no-communication or single-agent-vs-scripted-rival baseline to show silent above-Nash pricing is coordination rather than a default pricing prior.
Single provider; no non-Anthropic model in any regime.
Seeds fix matching only; API sampling at temperature 1 is unseeded, and no rerun with fresh seeds shows scorecard stability.
Agents' recorded reasons not analysed, so the expected-cost mechanism in the Discussion is untested.
Human comparison confounded (points vs euros, no trial periods, reworded instructions) without any calibration of these deviations.
Pre-registration commit and call records are self-attested; no external timestamp or signed hash a third party can verify.
No power argument for 4 pool sessions; Result 3 fails on interval width, not direction.

fixes_under_two_hours.fix: Reconcile all numeric contradictions (leniency 3/7 vs 9 and 2,400 points, reward interval in panel 2, panel 7 human value, NoReport sign).
Repair Table 3 layout (Calls and USD columns wrap digit by digit) and enlarge or move the overlapping difference annotations in Figure 1.
Qualify headline claims: state the placebo split in abstract and title, label Sonnet result exploratory, drop 'first' and 'any model'.
Shorten the title to under 15 words and add a three-bullet findings box after the introduction.
Add to Limitations: missing Sonnet no-channel baseline, unseeded sampling, human-comparison confounds; give the pre-registration as a verifiable public tag.

biggest_risk: The paper sells rigor, yet visible numeric contradictions (leniency convictions, figure vs table values) plus a broken Table 3 make a careful judge distrust every number and drop execution.
three_questions: Does Sonnet price above Nash against a scripted Nash rival or in a no-channel arm? Otherwise, how do you tell silent coordination from a pricing prior?
Table 3 lists 9 leniency convictions as 3 detections and 7 reports, with 2,400 points of fines; which numbers are correct?
How can a third party verify that the pre-registration and call records were not rewritten after the runs: signed tags, external timestamps, record hashes?
